StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

InstanceType.issue: PowerInstanceType.InstancedPerApplier (StranglePower.cs:29) -- and per power_cmd gap G5's corrected census this is the ONLY ported InstancedPerApplier power in the game (the other is OblivionPower, unported). The sim keys stacking on the power id alone (cmds.py:308), so two appliers' Strangles on one target merge into a single instance with a single `_amounts` dict and a single amount, where C# keeps one instance per applier -- each of which deals its own damage per card play. Mechanism owned by power_cmd G5; not re-verdicted (rule 3). DORMANT in Ironclad scope: the only ported applier is the player, via Mad Science's Choking rider (cards/mad_science.py:128-130, `applier=ctx.player`), and there is exactly one player, so a second applier needs multiplayer or a monster-applied Strangle -- neither of which exists. This is the cleanest available statement of G5's InstancedPerApplier half: it is dormant *by scope*, not by content, so it will not become live by porting more Ironclad content. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

BeforeCardPlayed.rationale: StranglePower.cs:36-48 records `amountsForPlayedCards[cardPlay.Card] = base.Amount` for each card the applier's player plays; powers.py:2853-2856 keeps `self._amounts[id(card)] = self.amount`. The two C# guards -- `base.Applier?.Player == null` and `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Applier.Player` -- are single-player tautologies here because the only applier is the player. The DESIGN INTENT is preserved and is the subtle part: recording at BeforeCardPlayed is what stops Strangle triggering on the very card that applied it, since that card is already past its own BeforeCardPlayed -- the source's own comment (StranglePower.cs:18-21) says so and the sim's (powers.py:2849-2852) repeats it.

AfterCardPlayed.issue: The damage TYPING is exact -- C# is `ValueProp.Unblockable | ValueProp.Unpowered` with dealer null and cardSource null (StranglePower.cs:55) and the sim passes `props=DamageProps.NON_CARD_HP_LOSS`, which valueprops.py:44 defines as exactly `UNBLOCKABLE | UNPOWERED`, with no dealer and no card. That is the recurring omitted-`props` shape (power report section 4 item 4) got RIGHT, and it is worth recording as such. The gap is hook_dispatch gap G4, the per-CardPlay bracket: CardModel.cs:1904-1965 builds a fresh CardPlay per Replay iteration and fires BeforeCardPlayed at :1929 and AfterCardPlayed at :1959 INSIDE the `for (int i = 0; i < playCount; i++)` loop, so a doubled card runs Add-then-Remove twice and Strangle deals its damage TWICE; combat.py:466 fires before_card_played once before the `for _ in range(play_count)` loop and combat.py:514 fires on_card_played once after it, so the sim deals it ONCE. G4 is already LIVE with an executed witness and is not re-verdicted; the per-unit consequence is N-times-less Strangle damage on any replayed card. Co-occurrence is reachable: Strangle comes from Mad Science (the ported Act-3 Glory event Tinker Time) and the ported replay sources are Throwing Axe (the Act-3 Tanx shrine), One-Two Punch (powers.py:966), Duplication (powers.py:3919) and two enchantments. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.rationale: Correct slot. The owner is an ENEMY -- Mad Science applies Strangle to its target (cards/mad_science.py:128-130) -- so C#'s `participants.Contains(base.Owner)` (StranglePower.cs:61) selects the enemy side, and Hook.AfterTurnEnd for the enemy side (Hook.cs:1267, CombatManager.cs:1256) is the sim's on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345). Same correct-slot shape as tainted / high_voltage / territorial, and it means Strangle survives the whole enemy turn as C# intends. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: Strangle overrides no AfterRemoved, so the observable is identical -- the same mechanism note as power/no_draw's and power/tainted's.

guards.what: StranglePower.cs:52 `amountsForPlayedCards.Remove(card, out value)` keyed by CardModel
guards.rationale: The sim keys by `id(card)` (powers.py:2853, 2859). Equivalent for live cards -- the entry is written and popped inside one card play, so the object cannot be collected and its id cannot be recycled in between. Recorded because an id()-keyed dict is exactly the sort of shortcut that would be a gap if the entry outlived the play.

guards.what: powers.py:2860 `self.owner.is_gone` -> return, added by the sim
guards.rationale: C# has no such test; it relies on CreatureCmd.Damage refusing a dead target (damage_pipeline's step 1). The sim's check is earlier but the outcome is the same, and the dict entry is popped before the check on both sides, so no stale entry survives.

guards.what: The amount snapshot: damage = the amount AT BeforeCardPlayed, not at resolution
guards.rationale: C# stores base.Amount at BeforeCardPlayed and deals THAT value (StranglePower.cs:46, 55); powers.py:2856, 2859-2866 does the same. This is what makes a Strangle stacked mid-play deal the old amount, and it is preserved.
